comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
Ages are not related to entering 'special' ports. Like San Francisco and St. Petersburg, you only need to discover it via quests (and excluding SF, charting one sea zone) in order to reach the port in question. The steps to entering Port Royal are:

Complete the quest "Country of Pirates" - 7-star quest from Santo Domingo Maritime guild; just involves talking to NPCs in Nassau (1m entry fee for non-pirates) and Jamaica

Chart the Antilles Sea (must have already begun the Mercator world atlas quest for this option)

Those steps can be done in either order you please. "Country of Pirates" can be shared with fleetmates, but doesn't seem to appear again after having completed it once, so those who've gone and done it beforehand cannot pull the quest and share it again with others.

Either way, once "Country of Pirates" is finished, and the Antilles Sea charted, you then need to look for and complete the quest "Commission from Port Royal", a 6-star difficulty 17th Century P.4 Chrono quest from Santo Domingo's Maritime guild. This quest CANNOT be shared with others, so you'll need to pull it yourself; it showed for a friend with about 10k-ish or so battle fame, so it shouldn't be too hard to do.

Be advised that defeating a single NPC warship is necessary to complete the "Commission" quest. Amulets of the Sun can be used if your Maritime strength is lacking (as mine was). The first quest related visit to PR is free, but a 1m entry fee will be charged to enter it at other times, since it's considered a pirate port, the same as Nassau and Jolo. Quests to Port Royal always reward you with enough ducats to cover the entry fee, though, so no worries. Oh, and there's no barmaid in town, so completed quests cannot be reported within Port Royal.

Source: comments from the Grand Admiral job page

comments.author: sspb
comments.body: You don't need to actually complete the "Commission from Port Royal" quest in order to open up Port Royal. Once you have the discovery, you can abandon the quest and still be able to access the port in the future.
